record.context_brief: Logical definability of orders in tournaments
record.original_question: Fix a class of tournaments of bounded clique-width. Is there a constant number of colors and a CMSO-definable binary formula φ(x, y) such that, for every tournament T in the class, one can choose a coloring λ of the vertices so that φ interprets a total order on V(T), meaning that for all vertices x and y, x < y holds in that order exactly when the colored structure (T, λ) satisfies φ(x, y)?

evidence.quote: There exists c, and φ logical formula, such that for all tournament T there exists a total order on the vertices, a coloring λ such that x < y iff T,λ satifies φ(x, y).
Does it work for a class of tournaments with bounded clique-width and CMSO logic ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let CMSO denote counting monadic second-order logic over relational structures. A tournament is a directed graph T=(V(T),E(T)) such that for every pair of distinct vertices x,y exactly one of (x,y) or (y,x) belongs to E(T). The clique-width of a tournament is defined analogously to the undirected case, using the operations of introducing a single-labeled vertex, taking disjoint union, adding all arcs in one direction between vertices of two given labels, and relabeling.

Given a finite set C of colors, a C-coloring of T is a map λ:V(T)→C; the resulting structure (T,λ) is regarded as a relational structure equipping the tournament with unary predicates indexed by C. A CMSO formula φ(x,y) with two free first-order variables and access to the predicates of (T,λ) interprets a total order on V(T) if the binary relation

  { (x,y) ∈ V(T)×V(T) : (T,λ) ⊨ φ(x,y) }

is a strict total order on V(T).

Question: Fix a class 𝒞 of tournaments of bounded clique-width. Do there exist a finite set of colors C and a CMSO formula φ(x,y) such that, for every tournament T ∈ 𝒞, one can choose a coloring λ:V(T)→C with the property that φ interprets a total order on V(T) inside (T,λ)?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Geniet, Ghasemi, Kanté, "Transducing Linear Decompositions of Tournaments", 2026) establishes that linear clique-decompositions of bounded width can be produced by a first-order transduction on tournaments of bounded linear clique-width, which yields CMSO-definable orderings in that linear setting and gives an equivalence between CMSO and existential MSO there. The general bounded clique-width (non-linear) case for tournaments does not appear to be settled in the located sources, so the status is reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Transducing Linear Decompositions of Tournaments
status_evidence.snippet: We show that in the case of tournaments, a first-order transduction suffices. This implies that the logics CMSO and existential MSO are equivalent over bounded linear clique-width tournaments.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the linear clique-width variant via a first-order transduction producing linear decompositions, hence CMSO-definable orderings in that case.

status_evidence.title: Definable decompositions for graphs of bounded linear cliquewidth
status_evidence.snippet: Bojańczyk–Pilipczuk–Grohe: clique-decompositions of bounded width can be produced by a CMSO transduction on graphs of bounded linear clique-width.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the analogous CMSO-transduction result for undirected graphs of bounded linear clique-width, motivating the tournament question.
